summary: City-owned 1933 harbor light in Lakeside Park, Fond du Lac, built by donation during the Depression; saved 1967, closed 2021, reopened 2023.

structures.type: eight-sided frame tower on a flagstone base
structures.note: 40 ft (12.2 m) per the Wisconsin Historical Society, LighthouseFriends and Penberthy; Rowlett gives 56 ft (17 m) (see notes_for_editor)

access.note: In Lakeside Park, reached by road with parking. Tower open to self-guided tours in season (usually Memorial Day to Labor Day).

events.note: Lumberman W. J. Nuss offered to build a lighthouse in Lakeside Park; the park board accepted
Construction from May 1933; cornerstone 10 July 1933; top stairs finished October 1933
Park superintendent reported the first two floors weakened and the top deck and railing in poor condition (LighthouseFriends, from a 1965 newspaper)
Restoration drive begun; city paid most of about $8,000 in repairs
Rededicated and opened again on 3 July 1968
Plaque reads 'Restored 1993'; Rowlett also gives 1968 and 1993
Closed to the public in September 2021 for water damage and other repairs
Access back in 2023 after renovations; a ribbon-cutting for the Lakeside Park improvements was set for 29 June (the 28 June 2023 article announces it, so the date it was held is not confirmed)

notes_for_editor: (1) Height: the Wisconsin Historical Society, LighthouseFriends and Penberthy give 40 feet (12.2 m); Rowlett gives 56 ft (17 m) and a 60 ft (18 m) focal plane; the record's 17.0 m and Wikipedia's 56 ft (17 m) follow Rowlett. Not corrected here because the sources disagree and no measurement was read; the story states both. (2) The 2026 blog's WPA attribution is second-hand from a sign; LighthouseFriends says only 'out-of-work' citizens. The story says so. (3) Restoration dates conflict or overlap: LighthouseFriends' plaque ('Saved 1967, Restored 1993'), Penberthy's 1966 drive and 1968 rededication, and Rowlett's '1968 and 1993'. The story reports each as its source gives it. (4) Keepers: none named in any source read; the roster returns none. (5) The 1965 Commonwealth Reporter item is cited only as LighthouseFriends prints it. (6) Wikipedia (lead only) says the light was constructed 1933 with a 17 m tower and a 'Pending major rebuild' note; not used. (7) The record's 'active' status is consistent with Rowlett ('Active (maintained by City of Fond du Lac)') and the Wisconsin Historical Society's note that the original beacon still lines up with another beacon. (8) The record's characteristic 'FI R' is not quoted in any source read; Rowlett says 'flashing red light', so no characteristic is entered. (9) Not a Coast Guard or federal light as far as the sources show: the city owns and maintains it. (10) No storms, wrecks or rescues tied to the station in sources read; that chapter is omitted. (11) Fact check 2026-10-28: the 2026 blog's WPA claim is kept in the story, flagged as unconfirmed. The WPA was created in 1935, two years after the 1933 build, so the claim conflicts with the build date; a human should decide whether to keep it. The 2023 reopening is stated as 2023 because the 28 June article says access is back this year.
